source: the structure of the ring sheet below and among the measured knots of ringfield.json: a ladder of octaves of ringlets by radius (plateaus with jittered edges; at each edge a groove and the slope of the step as a thin line), wave trains, and the hue each ringlet takes. Lengths in planet radii. Read by field.ts. The strengths per octave are set from the contrast by scale of the two approved images (assets-src/saturn/code/band_energy.py).
note: per octave, from the widest. level: how far a ringlet moves the logarithm of the brightness, in the dense rings and in the thin ones. slope: how bright the slope lines are when they face the Sun. tau is the share of the level that also moves the optical depth. rough and bunch: ringlets come in bunches, the strength of an octave runs between the two values of rough with a field that changes two octaves more slowly, over the two thresholds of bunch. edge is the half width of the edge of a ringlet in cells: the two widest octaves are soft zones of colour. filterFloor: the ladder is filtered with the pixel's footprint over the root of the samples of a frame, but never with less than this share of a pixel.

groove.note: the thin lines at the edges of the ringlets: half width in cells, narrowest and widest; the share of the range of strengths that gives no line; how far a dark line and a bright line move the logarithm of the brightness and how far a line moves the logarithm of the optical depth, per unit of strength; the strength per octave, and its gain in the dense and in the thin rings

hue.note: how far a ringlet moves the colour along two axes (warm to cool, rose to green), per octave from the widest, in the dense rings and in the thin ones

waves.note: each train: radius of the resonance, length, wavelength at its far end, 1 for outward and -1 for inward. rise and fall are fractions of the length; tight caps how short the waves get near the resonance.
